data: Vostok-K successor — more thrust for the heavier Voskhod capsule. Launched Voskhod 1 (1964) + Voskhod 2 (1965 Leonov EVA)

Voskhod (GRAU index 11A57) was the next iteration of the R-7 family after Vostok-K, with uprated Blok-I third-stage engines for the heavier Voskhod capsule. Three-stage LOX + kerosene, 44 metres tall, 298 tonnes lift-off mass. Launched both crewed Voskhod flights (Voskhod 1 first 3-person crew in 1964; Voskhod 2 with Leonov's first EVA in 1965). After the Voskhod programme ended the 11A57 continued in service for ~300 uncrewed military / civilian satellite launches through 1976, when it was superseded by the Soyuz 11A511 line.

The Voskhod 11A57 was the R-7 turned up a notch. The modified Vostok capsule was heavier than the original, so it needed more push than the Vostok-K could give — which the R-7 family, endlessly adaptable, duly provided with an uprated upper stage. It's a small chapter in a very long story: the same basic rocket that launched Sputnik and Gagarin, stretched again to loft the two Voskhod flights, and still being stretched, decades later, to fly Soyuz crews. Few designs have been asked to do so many different jobs for so long.
First multi-crew spaceflight — three cosmonauts in a Vostok-derived capsule
Sputnik 1 (1957). Vostok 1 — Gagarin (1961). Five hundred and forty Soyuz launches from a single pad.
